D_vikings_cover_standard.text: COVER PRODUCTION STANDARD: This is a finished full-color portrait comic-book cover, not an interior story page. Sell one dominant issue-specific contradiction, desire or pressure in one glance. Preserve Vikings 2026's grounded painted documentary-comedy realism, human dignity, ordinary present-day New York, clean focal hierarchy and strong thumbnail readability. Prefer iconic issue-specific staging over recap collage. The central Norse figures should usually look unmistakably out of place because they are materially and behaviorally ninth-century people inside modern civic life; do not neutralize that contrast by modernizing their posture, costume language, gear, or reactions. When the cover occurs in public, New Yorkers around them should usually continue ordinary business—commuting, waiting, working, reading, carrying groceries, drinking coffee, checking phones, handling customers—without stopping to stare, point, laugh, photograph, or form a reaction crowd. The city should absorb the strangeness by continuing. Background indifference must remain secondary to the issue hook: it enriches the image but never becomes a gag panel. Humor must come from incompatible systems and ordinary New York indifference rather than making the displaced Norse characters look foolish. Do not default to generic cast lineups, floating-head montage, fake action, decorative runes, fantasy spectacle, caricature, or invented promotional clutter. Preserve a clean masthead/trade-dress field. Do not reveal later issue solutions, reversals, rulings or end-state payoffs beyond the recipe's explicit spoiler ceiling.

D_vikings_cover_trade_dress.text: COVER TRADE-DRESS REFERENCE GATE: Before generating any Vikings 2026 cover, retrieve and visually pixel-read the approved local Issue 1 reference at production/references/vikings-2026/assets/covers/issue-01-cover-trade-dress.jpg. It is an exact copy of the released StarSplitterVisions Issue 1 cover and is the publication-design authority. Preserve its intentionally dull municipal-publication character: a large plain white upper field; boxed Star Splitter / VISIONS publisher mark at upper left; year-and-issue block within that badge; huge dark condensed VIKINGS 2026! wordmark; thin horizontal rules; narrow all-caps strapline beneath the wordmark; restrained dark navy/black ink; rigid alignment; generous institutional white space; and the hard transition from bureaucratic masthead into painted cover art. The masthead should feel closer to a City of New York agency bulletin, public-information handout, annual report, or municipal case publication than to a flashy commercial comic. Do not add metallic type, faux-Norse lettering, distressed textures, gradients, glow, drop shadows, speed effects, dramatic diagonals, price bursts, taglines, blurbs, barcodes, creator splashes, or other commercial-comic excitement. The top should remain almost humorlessly official and visually boring on purpose; the image beneath it is the sales engine. Use the Issue 1 pixels for cover branding only. Do NOT copy Issue 1's waiting-room scene composition, character arrangement, camera angle, background or issue-specific art into later covers unless the current cover recipe independently requires it. The current issue recipe controls the selling image.
